audits.title: A Closed-Loop Audit of Thrombo-Embolic Deterrent Stocking Use in an Orthopaedic Ward.
audits.setting: Orthopaedic specialty ward of a teaching hospital in Dublin

cycle1.result: 11 (55%) patients wearing TEDS correctly; 13 (65%) educated on the importance of TEDS.

audits.intervention: Educational intervention reminding ward staff to monitor TEDS adherence and educate patients, plus an educational poster.

cycle2.result: 18 (90%) patients wearing TEDS correctly; 16 (80%) properly educated.

audits.citation: Lim B, Mc Kenna J. A Closed-Loop Audit of Thrombo-Embolic Deterrent Stocking Use in an Orthopaedic Ward. . 2024. doi:10.14293/pr2199.000761.v1.

audits.title: Is there adequate provision of venous thromboembolism prophylaxis following hip arthroplasty? An audit and international survey.
audits.standard: Evidence-based guidelines recommending VTE prophylaxis for 4 weeks after hip arthroplasty
audits.setting: Adult Lower Extremity Reconstruction, Mount Sinai Hospital, Toronto

cycle1.result: Enoxaparin 40 mg once daily: mean duration of prophylaxis 5.4 days.

audits.intervention: Switch to oral rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily.

cycle2.result: Rivaroxaban: mean duration of prophylaxis 35 days.

audits.other_findings: International survey: 4 of 39 (10.2%) units prescribing LMWH did so for at least 4 weeks.
audits.citation: Rogers BA, Phillips S, Foote J, Drabu KJ. Is there adequate provision of venous thromboembolism prophylaxis following hip arthroplasty? An audit and international survey. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2010;92(8):668-672. doi:10.1308/003588410x12699663904952. PMID: 20615303.

audits.title: Trimodal venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in total knee replacement: A quality improvement project for best care practices.
audits.standard: National guidelines for risk stratification and trimodal VTE prophylaxis (chemical, mechanical, early ambulation)
audits.setting: Tertiary facility in central Massachusetts, total knee replacement patients

cycle1.result: Frontline staff negligence identified as the main cause of nonadherence in the mechanical arm (figures not given in the supplied text).

audits.other_findings: Unannounced mechanical prophylaxis adherence audits supplemented documented data.

audits.title: Venous thromboembolism rates in patients with lower limb immobilization after Achilles tendon injury are unchanged after the introduction of prophylactic aspirin: audit.
audits.standard: Local policy to routinely prescribe aspirin 100 mg daily for Achilles tendon injury requiring lower limb immobilisation

cycle1.result: Aspirin prescribed in 0.5%; symptomatic VTE incidence 6.3%.

audits.intervention: Introduction of a policy to routinely prescribe aspirin 100 mg daily

cycle2.result: Aspirin prescribed to 189/218 (93%); symptomatic VTE in 14 (6.4%, 95% CI 3.6-10.5%), unchanged.

audits.other_findings: All patients who developed VTE had been prescribed aspirin; authors suggest considering LMWH instead.
audits.citation: Braithwaite I, Dunbar L, Eathorne A, Weatherall M, Beasley R. Venous thromboembolism rates in patients with lower limb immobilization after Achilles tendon injury are unchanged after the introduction of prophylactic aspirin: audit. J Thromb Haemost. 2016;14(2):331-335. doi:10.1111/jth.13224. PMID: 26663418.

audits.title: Medical rota changes and venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in orthopaedic patients.
audits.standard: SIGN guideline 122 VTE prophylaxis; seven-item checklist (weight/BMI and eGFR recorded, correct LMWH dose, timely administration, AES prescribed and worn, early mobilisation, hydration), 100% target
audits.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic unit, Monklands District General Hospital, NHS Lanarkshire (emergency admissions)

cycle1.result: 71% of patients compliant with all measures; errors mainly medical (failure to prescribe LMWH or stockings, incorrect dosing), plus nursing and patient errors; about 30% of surveyed patients (n=47) understood aims of VTE prophylaxis.

audits.intervention: Policy of prophylaxis unless contraindicated, summarised guidelines displayed on wards, MDT teaching for doctors and nurses, patient education, VTE added to handover and radiology meeting, teaching after rota change, and VTE education added to junior doctor induction.

cycle2.result: Re-audit 4: 100% compliance; 80% of patients understood aims of VTE prophylaxis.

audits.other_findings: Re-audits: 93% (n=27), 100% (n=26), 86% (n=22, dip after medical staff rotation), 100% (n=25); spot audit six months later showed 100%.
audits.citation: Bohler I, George Mackenzie Jardine A. Medical rota changes and venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in orthopaedic patients. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;3(1):u206652.w2672. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u206652.w2672. PMID: 26734265.

audits.title: Intervention to Improve Compliance With National Guidelines on Venous Thromboembolism Chemoprophylaxis for Patients With Operatively Managed Ankle Fractures.
audits.standard: NICE guidance on pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for ankle surgery with immobilisation, and BOAST requirement that VTE prophylaxis follows agreed local protocols; no target stated
audits.setting: Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust, single centre, operatively managed ankle fractures

cycle1.result: Operation note documentation of VTE chemoprophylaxis: agent and duration specified 40 (29%), nonspecific 40 (29%), none 57 (42%). Discharged with VTE chemoprophylaxis 78 (57%).

audits.intervention: Quality Improvement Half-Day educating surgeons and ward junior doctors; new written local policy of enoxaparin 40 mg once daily for 6 weeks for all operatively managed ankle fractures unless contraindicated; posters for 3 weeks in theatre and ward areas; review of prophylaxis at 2- and 6-week clinics.

cycle2.result: Operation note agent and duration specified 44 (90%), nonspecific 3 (6%), none 2 (4%) (all P<0.001). Discharged with VTE chemoprophylaxis 48 (98%) (P<0.001).

audits.other_findings: In cycle 1, discharge prophylaxis was 97.2% when agent and duration were in the operation note versus 51.8% with nonspecific and 32.4% with no documentation (P<0.001). Two VTE events (one DVT, one PE) occurred in cycle 1 and none in cycle 2.
audits.citation: Burnett-Jones L, Srinivasan A, Mead A, Malik A. Intervention to Improve Compliance With National Guidelines on Venous Thromboembolism Chemoprophylaxis for Patients With Operatively Managed Ankle Fractures. Ochsner J. 2022;22(4):319-323. doi:10.31486/toj.22.0038. PMID: 36561096.

audits.title: Evaluating the Compliance to 24-Hour Venous Thromboembolism Risk Re-assessment Following Orthopaedic Surgery at a Tertiary Center: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: NICE VTE guideline (over 16s): VTE risk reassessment within 24 hours after surgery; target 100%
audits.setting: Tertiary elective orthopaedic hospital, Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, London

cycle1.result: 6/4780 (0.13%) had VTE reassessment completed within 24 hours of surgery.

audits.intervention: Automated system prompt on EPMA reminding staff to complete VTE reassessment 24 hours after surgery.

cycle2.result: 112/156 (74%) completed within 24 hours (p<0.0001); 131/156 (83%) completed at any time.

audits.other_findings: Initial VTE assessment compliance was high because it is a mandatory step on EPMA.
audits.citation: Imtiaz H, Nguyen TV, Vy Thai TT, Kouklidis G, Horgan M, Vijayaraghavan R. Evaluating the Compliance to 24-Hour Venous Thromboembolism Risk Re-assessment Following Orthopaedic Surgery at a Tertiary Center: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit. Cureus. 2024;16(11):e74882. doi:10.7759/cureus.74882. PMID: 39618767.

audits.title: Improving Patient Care and Clinical Services: Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis After Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
audits.standard: NICE VTE guidance: THR 28 days LMWH plus anti-embolism stockings until discharge; TKR 14 days LMWH plus stockings
audits.setting: Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley (district general hospital); elective total hip and knee replacement discharge summaries

cycle1.result: THR 23/25 (92%) and TKR 20/23 (87%) received enoxaparin plus stockings; overall compliance 90%.

audits.intervention: Arthroplasty discharge pack displayed as posters and handouts at the arthroplasty station, regular teaching sessions on NICE discharge guidance, and final check of discharge letters by the nurse in charge.

cycle2.result: THR 24/24 (100%) and TKR 22/23 (96%) correct; overall compliance 98%.

audits.other_findings: Overall compliance was calculated as the average of the THR and TKR rates; patient outcomes were not recorded.
audits.citation: Mussab RM, Venkatesan M, Khan IA, Raja V, Kothari S. Improving Patient Care and Clinical Services: Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis After Hip and Knee Arthroplasty. Cureus. 2025;17(6):e86448. doi:10.7759/cureus.86448. PMID: 40688888.

audits.title: Post-operative Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis for Non-arthroplasty Knee Surgery: A Closed Loop Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: NICE VTE guidance: prophylaxis after arthroscopy if anaesthetic time 90 minutes or more (or VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk), and after all other non-arthroplasty knee surgery; target 100%
audits.setting: Joint replacement unit, tertiary orthopaedic hospital (University Hospitals Dorset / Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital affiliations); elective non-arthroplasty knee procedures

cycle1.result: Arthroscopy with anaesthetic time >90 minutes 2/4 (50%) received prophylaxis; other non-arthroplasty surgery 9/25 (36%).

audits.intervention: Formal teaching session for the joint replacement unit team by a senior consultant on recording anaesthetic time, weight-bearing status and VTE prescription on operation notes and postoperative instructions.
audits.other_findings: No VTE events were reported. The text states both 56 and 66 patients for the second loop; authors suggest a VTE checklist with discharge summaries.
audits.citation: Imtiaz H, Anaga E, Kouklidis G, Horgan M. Post-operative Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis for Non-arthroplasty Knee Surgery: A Closed Loop Clinical Audit. Cureus. 2025;17(8):e89461. doi:10.7759/cureus.89461. PMID: 40918921.

audits.title: Audit of thromboembolic prophylaxis in hip and knee surgery.
audits.standard: Departmental thromboembolic prophylaxis policy (TED stockings, subcutaneous low-dose heparin, PEP trial inclusion for fractured neck of femur)
audits.setting: Orthopaedic department, St James's University Hospital, Leeds

cycle1.result: Subcutaneous heparin given in 43% of primary and 14% of revision hip replacements; all knee replacements received heparin but 75% at incorrect dose. Hip fracture: TED stockings 0% to 70%, heparin 0% to 20%, PEP trial inclusion 0% to 20%.

cycle2.result: Statistically significant improvement in subcutaneous heparin and TED stocking use in arthroplasty and in PEP trial inclusion of hip fracture patients.

audits.citation: Williams HR, Macdonald DA. Audit of thromboembolic prophylaxis in hip and knee surgery. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 1997;79(1):55-57. PMID: 9038497.
